standard_prerequisites.name: Points of a localized topos give points of the ambient topos
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the points obtained by composing with the localization and the identification of the resulting stalks.

standard_prerequisites.name: Conservative families of points
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definition of a conservative family of points and Lemma lemma-exactness-stalks

core_obligations: Construction of the points (proof lines 9394-9401): for each localization a conservative family of points is chosen, and composing with the localization morphism gives points of the ambient site.

The family is conservative (proof lines 9402-9420): for a map of sheaves which is an isomorphism at all the constructed points, the author uses the covering assumption to reduce to objects mapping into one of the chosen objects, where the restriction is an isomorphism because the chosen family on that localization is conservative, and then concludes by the sheaf condition.
proof_roadmap: Compose the conservative families of the localizations with the localizations.
Show that a map which is an isomorphism at all these points is one locally.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a site has enough points provided that the sheaves represented by a family of objects cover the final object and each localization has enough points (statement lines 9382-9391). The proof is a complete argument: conservative families of points of the localizations are composed with the localization morphisms to give points of the ambient site (proof lines 9394-9401); and the resulting family is shown to be conservative by reducing, via the covering assumption, to objects mapping into one of the chosen objects, where the restriction is an isomorphism by conservativity of the chosen family, after which the sheaf condition concludes (proof lines 9402-9420). The non-formal content is the local-to-global step. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
